questions.q: If $a\gt0, b\gt0, c\gt0$ and $a, b, c$ are distinct, then $(a+b)(b+c)(c+a)$ is greater than
questions.solution:
We know that $\mathrm{AM} \geq \mathrm{GM}$...(i)
Now, applying Eq. (i) in $a$ and $b\Rightarrow \quad \frac{a+b}{2} \geq \sqrt{a b}$....(ii)
applying Eq. (i) in $b$ and $c\Rightarrow \quad \frac{b+c}{2} \geq \sqrt{b c}$....(iii)
and applying Eq. (i) in $c$ and $a\Rightarrow \quad \frac{c+a}{2} \geq \sqrt{c a}$....(iv)
By E'qs. (ii), (iii) and (iv)
$\begin{array}{cc}
\Rightarrow & \frac{(a+b)(b+c)(c+a)}{8} \geq a b c \\
\Rightarrow & (a+b)(b+c)(c+a) \geq 8 a b c
\end{array}$

questions.q: If $\sum_{k=1}^n k(k+1)(k-1)=p n^4+q n^3+t n^2+s n$ where $p, q, t$ and $s$ are constants, then the value of $s$ is equal to
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}
\text { Let } S & =\sum_{k=1}^n k(k+1)(k-1) \\
& =\sum_{k=1}^n k^3-k
\end{aligned}$
We know that
$\sum_{r=1}^P r=\frac{P(P+1)}{2}$
and
$\sum_{r=1}^P r^3=\left[\frac{P(P+1)}{2}\right]^2\begin{aligned}
S & =\left[\frac{n(n+1)}{2}\right]^2-\left[\frac{n(n+1)}{2}\right] \\
& =\frac{n(n+1)}{2}\left[\frac{n(n+1)}{2}-1\right] \\
& =\left(\frac{n^2+n}{2}\right)\left[\frac{n^2+n-2}{2}\right] \\
& =\frac{n^4}{4}+\frac{n^3}{2}-\frac{n^2}{4}-\frac{n}{2}...(i)
\end{aligned}$
Now, by comparing $p n^4+q n^3+t n^2+s n$ with Eq. (i),
$S=-\frac{1}{2}$

equal to
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \text { Given } \tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{1+1.2}\right)+\tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{1+2.3}\right)+\ldots \\ & +\tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{1+n(n+1)}\right)=\tan ^{-1}(x)\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} \Rightarrow \tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{2-1}{1+1.2}\right) & +\tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{3-2}{1+2.3}\right)+\ldots \\ & +\tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{n+1-n}{1+n(n+1)}\right)=\tan ^{-1}(x)\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \tan ^{-1}(2)-\tan ^{-1}(1)+\tan ^{-1}(3)-\tan ^{-1}(2)+\ldots \\ & +\tan ^{-1}(\mathrm{n}+1)-\tan ^{-1}(\mathrm{n})=\tan ^{-1}(x)\end{aligned}\Rightarrow \tan ^{-1}(\mathrm{n}+1)-\tan ^{-1}(1)=\tan ^{-1}(x)\left\{\because \tan ^{-1}(A)-\tan ^{-1}(B)=\tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{A-B}{1+A \cdot B}\right)\right\}\Rightarrow \tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{n}{n+2}\right)=\tan ^{-1}(x) \Rightarrow x=\frac{n}{n+2}$

questions.q: If arithmetic mean of two distinct positive real number $a$ and $b(a \gt b)$ be twice their geometric mean, then $a: b=$
questions.solution:
By the given condition,
$\frac{a+b}{2}=2 \sqrt{a b} \Rightarrow a+b=4 \sqrt{a b}$
Now, $(a-b)^2=(a+b)^2-4 a b=16 a b-4 a b=12 a b\therefore a-b=\sqrt{12 a b}=2 \sqrt{3} \sqrt{a b}$.
(Taking + ve sign only as $a \gt b$)
$\therefore \frac{a+b}{a-b}=\frac{4 \sqrt{a b}}{2 \sqrt{3} \sqrt{a b}}=\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}$
By componendo and dividendo,
$\frac{2 a}{2 b}=\frac{2+\sqrt{3}}{2-\sqrt{3}}$ or $\frac{a}{b}=\frac{2+\sqrt{3}}{2-\sqrt{3}}$

questions.q: If $y=\tan ^{-1} \frac{1}{x^2+x+1}+\tan ^{-1} \frac{1}{x^2+3 x+3}+\tan ^{-1} \frac{1}{x^2+5 x+7}+\ldots$.to $n$ terms, then $\frac{d y}{d x}=$
questions.solution:
Given, $y=\tan ^{-1} \frac{1}{x^2+x+1}+\tan ^{-1} \frac{1}{x^2+3 x+3}+\tan ^{-1} \frac{1}{x^2+5 x+7}+\cdots \cdot$
to $n$ terms
$=\tan ^{-1}\left\{\frac{1}{1+x(x+1)}\right\}+\tan ^{-1}\left\{\frac{1}{1+(x+1)(x+2)}\right\}+\tan ^{-1}\left\{\frac{1}{1+(x+2)(x+3)}\right\}+\ldots \ldots \ldots+\tan ^{-1}\left\{\frac{1}{1+(x+(n-1))(x+n)}\right\}=\tan ^{-1}\left\{\frac{(x+1)-x}{1+(x+1) x}\right\}+\tan ^{-1}\left\{\frac{(x+2)-(x+1)}{1+(x+2)(x+1)}\right\}+\tan ^{-1}\left\{\frac{(x+3)-(x+2)}{1+(x+3)(x+2)}\right\}+\ldots .+\tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{(x+n)-(x+n-1)}{1+(x+n)(x+n-1)}\right)\therefore y=\left\{\tan ^{-1}(x+1)-\tan ^{-1}(x)\right\}+\left\{\tan ^{-1}(x+2)-\tan ^{-1}(x+1)\right\}+\left\{\tan ^{-1}(x+3)-\tan ^{-1}(x+2)\right\}+\ldots \ldots . .+\left\{\tan ^{-1}(x+n)-\tan ^{-1}[x+(n-1)]\right\}$
So, $\quad y=\tan ^{-1}(x+n)-\tan ^{-1}(x)$
On differentiating both sides w.r.t. $x$, we get
$\frac{d y}{d x}=\frac{1}{1+(x+n)^2}-\frac{1}{1+x^2}$

questions.q: If the sum of an infinite GP $a, a r, a r^2, a r^3, \ldots$ is 15 and the sum of the squares of its each term is 150 , then the sum of $a r^2, a r^4, a r^6, \ldots$ is :
questions.solution:
Sum of infinite terms of series a $+a r+a r^2+=15$
$\therefore \frac{a}{1-r}=15$ ...(i)
Sequence formed by square of terms: $a^2, a^2 r^2, a^2 r^4, a^2 r^6 \ldots$
$a^2+a^2 r^2+\cdots=150$
Sum $=\frac{a^2}{1-r^2}=150$
$\Rightarrow \frac{a}{1-r} \cdot \frac{a}{1+r}=15 \Rightarrow 15 \cdot \frac{a}{1+r}=150\left(\because \frac{\mathrm{a}}{1-\mathrm{r}}=15\right)$
$\Rightarrow \frac{a}{1+r}=10$ ...(ii)
On dividing equation (i) by (ii)
$\frac{1+\mathrm{r}}{1-\mathrm{r}}=\frac{15}{10}$
or $r=\frac{1}{5} \Rightarrow a=12$
Now series : $a r^2+a r^4+a r^6+\ldots$
Sum $=\frac{a^2}{1-r^2}=\frac{12 \cdot\left(\frac{1}{25}\right)}{1-\frac{1}{25}}=\frac{1}{2}$

questions.q: Let $a_1, a_2, \ldots \ldots a_{40}$ be in AP and $h_1, h_2, \ldots . h_{10}$ be in HP. If $a_1=h_1=2$ and $a_{10}=h_{10}=3$, then $a_4 h_7$ is
questions.solution:
Let $d$ be the common difference of the AP. Then,
$\begin{aligned}
& a_{10}=3 \Rightarrow a_1+9 d=3 \\
\Rightarrow & 2+9 d=3 \Rightarrow d=\frac{1}{9} \\
\therefore & a_4=a_1+3 d=2+\frac{1}{3}=\frac{7}{3}
\end{aligned}$
Let $D$ be the common difference of $\frac{1}{h_1}, \frac{1}{h_2}, \ldots .-\frac{1}{h_{10}}$.
Then, $\quad h_{10}=3\begin{array}{ll}
\Rightarrow & \frac{1}{h_{10}}=\frac{1}{3} \Rightarrow \frac{1}{2}+9 D=\frac{1}{3} \\
\Rightarrow & 9 D=-\frac{1}{6} \Rightarrow D=-\frac{1}{54} \\
\therefore & \frac{1}{h_7}=\frac{1}{h_1}+6 D=\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{9}=\frac{7}{18} \\
\Rightarrow & h_7=\frac{18}{7} \\
\therefore & a_4 h_7=\frac{7}{3} \times \frac{18}{7}=6
\end{array}$

questions.q: Let $a_1, a_2, a_3 \ldots$ be a harmonic progression with $a_1=5$ and $a_{20}=25$. The least positive integer $n$ for which $a_n \lt  0$, is
questions.solution:
It is given that $a_1, a_2, a_3 \ldots$. are in HP. Therefore, $\frac{1}{a_1}, \frac{1}{a_2}, \frac{1}{a_3}, \ldots \ldots .$. are in AP. Let $d$ be the common difference of the AP.
$\therefore \quad \frac{1}{a_n}=\frac{1}{a_1}+(n-1) d$ and $\frac{1}{a_{20}}=\frac{1}{a_1}+19 d\Rightarrow \quad \frac{1}{a_n}=\frac{1}{5}+(n-1) d$ and $\frac{1}{25}=\frac{1}{5}+19 d\Rightarrow \quad \frac{1}{a_n}=\frac{1}{5}+(n-1) d$ and $d=\frac{-4}{19 \times 25}\Rightarrow \quad \frac{1}{a_n}=\frac{1}{5}-\frac{4(n-1)}{19 \times 25}\Rightarrow \quad \frac{1}{a_n}=\frac{95-4 n+4}{19 \times 25}\Rightarrow \quad a_n=\frac{99-4 n}{19 \times 25}$
Now, $a_n \lt  0\Rightarrow \quad \frac{99-4 n}{19 \times 25} \lt  0\Rightarrow \quad 99-4 n \lt  0\Rightarrow \quad 4 n\gt 99\Rightarrow \quad n\gt 24 \frac{3}{4} \Rightarrow n \geq 25$

If $\alpha, \beta, \gamma \in[0, \pi]$ and if $\alpha, \beta, \gamma$ are in AP, then 
$\frac{\sin \alpha-\sin \gamma}{\cos \gamma-\cos \alpha}$ is equal to
questions.solution:
$\frac{\sin \alpha-\sin \gamma}{\cos \gamma-\cos \alpha}=\frac{2 \cos \frac{\alpha+\gamma}{2} \sin \frac{\alpha-\gamma}{2}}{2 \sin \frac{\alpha+\gamma}{2} \cdot \sin \frac{\alpha-\gamma}{2}}=\cot \frac{\alpha+\gamma}{2}\left[\begin{array}{l}\because \sin A-\sin B=2 \cos \left(\frac{A+B}{2}\right) \sin \left(\frac{A-B}{2}\right) \\ \text { and } \cos A-\cos B=2 \sin \left(\frac{A+B}{2}\right) \sin \left(\frac{B-A}{2}\right)\end{array}\right]$
But $\alpha, \beta, \gamma$ are in $AP\Rightarrow \quad \frac{\alpha+\gamma}{2}=\beta$
So, required value is $\cot \beta$.

questions.q: The fourth term of an A.P. is three times of the first term and the seventh term exceeds the twice of the third term by one, then the common difference of the progression is
questions.solution:
Let the progression be $a$, $a+d$, a +2 d,

Then $x_{4}=3 x_{1} \Rightarrow a+3 d=3 a \Rightarrow 3 d=2 a \ldots$ (i)

Again $x_{7}=2 x_{3}+1\Rightarrow a+6 d=2(a+2 d)+1 \Rightarrow 2 d=a+1 \quad \ldots$ (ii)

Solving (i) and (ii), we get $\mathrm{a}=3, \mathrm{~d}=2$

questions.q:
If $\log$ a, $\log \mathrm{b}$, and $\log \mathrm{c}$ are in A.P. and also $\log$ a $-\log 2 b, \log 2 b-\log 3 c, \log 3 c-\log$ a are in A.P.,

then
options: $\mathrm{a}, \mathrm{b}, \mathrm{c}$ are the sides of a triangle
questions.solution:
\(\log \mathrm{a}, \log \mathrm{b}, \log \mathrm{c}\) are in A.P.

\(\begin{aligned}

&\Rightarrow 2 \log \mathrm{b}=\log \mathrm{a}+\log \mathrm{c} \\

&\Rightarrow \log \mathrm{b}^{2}=\log (\mathrm{ac}) \\

&\Rightarrow \mathrm{b}^{2}=\mathrm{ac} \Rightarrow \mathrm{a}, \mathrm{b}, \mathrm{c} \text { are in G.P. } \\

&\log \mathrm{a}-\log 2 \mathrm{~b}, \log 2 \mathrm{~b}-\log 3 \mathrm{c}, \log 3 \mathrm{c}-\log \text { a are in A.P. }

\end{aligned}\)

\(\Rightarrow 2(\log 2 b-\log 3 c)=(\log a-\log 2 b)+(\log 3 c-\log a)\)

\(\Rightarrow 3 \log 2 \mathrm{~b}=3 \log 3 \mathrm{c} \Rightarrow 2 \mathrm{~b}=3 \mathrm{c}\)

Now, \(b^{2}=a c \Rightarrow b^{2}=a \cdot \frac{2 b}{3} \Rightarrow b=\frac{2 a}{3}, c=\frac{4 a}{9}\)

\(\begin{aligned}

&\text { i.e., } a=a, b=\frac{2 a}{3}, c=\frac{4 a}{9} \\

&\Rightarrow a: b: c=1: \frac{2}{3}: \frac{4}{9}=9: 6: 4

\end{aligned}\)

Since, sum of any two is greater than the \(3^{\mathrm{rd}}, \mathrm{a}, \mathrm{b}, \mathrm{c}\) form a triangle.

questions.q: $\left(x+\frac{1}{x}\right)^{2}+\left(x^{2}+\frac{1}{x^{2}}\right)^{2}+\left(x^{3}+\frac{1}{x^{3}}\right)^{2} \quad \ldots .$ upto $n$ terms is
questions.solution:
The series is



\begin{array}{l}

\left(x^{2}+x^{4}+x^{6}+\ldots\right)+\left(\frac{1}{x^{2}}+\frac{1}{x^{4}}+\frac{1}{x^{6}}+\ldots\right) \\

+(2+2+\ldots . .) \\

=\frac{x^{2}\left(x^{2 n}-1\right)}{x^{2}-1}+\frac{\frac{1}{x^{2}}\left(1-\frac{1}{x^{2 n}}\right)}{1-\frac{1}{x^{2}}}+2 n \\

=\frac{x^{2}\left(x^{2 n}-1\right)}{x^{2}-1}+\frac{x^{2 n}-1}{\left(x^{2}-1\right) x^{2 n}}+2 n \\

=\frac{x^{2 n}-1}{x^{2}-1} \times \frac{x^{2 n+2}+1}{x^{2 n}}+2 n

\end{array}

questions.q: If $\omega$ is the complex cube root of unity, then the value of $\omega+\omega^{\left(\frac{1}{2}+\frac{3}{8}+\frac{9}{32}+\frac{27}{128}+\ldots\right)}$ is
questions.solution:
Consider $\frac{1}{2}+\frac{3}{8}+\frac{9}{32}+\frac{27}{128}+\ldots .$

Which can be written as



\frac{3^{0}}{2^{1}}+\frac{3^{1}}{2^{3}}+\frac{3^{2}}{2^{5}}+\frac{3^{3}}{2^{7}}+\ldots .

 $=\frac{1}{2}\left[1+\frac{3}{2^{2}}+\frac{3^{2}}{2^{4}}+\frac{3^{3}}{2^{6}}+\ldots .\right]$

Since $\left(1+\frac{3}{2^{2}}+\frac{3^{2}}{2^{4}}+_{--}-\right)$ is a G.P.

therfore by sum of infinite G.P, we have



=\frac{1}{2}\left[\frac{1}{1-\frac{3}{2^{2}}}\right]=\frac{1}{2}\left[\frac{1}{1-\frac{3}{4}}\right]=2



$\therefore \quad$ Given expression



\begin{array}{l}

=-1 \\

{\left[\because 1+\omega+\omega^{2}=0\right]}

\end{array}

questions.q: If binomial coefficients of three consecutive terms of $(1+x)^{2}$ are in $H P$, then the maximum value of $\mathrm{n}$ is
questions.solution:
Let the coefficients of rth, $(r+1)$ th, and (r $+$

2) th terms be in HP.

Then, $\frac{2}{\binom{n}{r}}=\frac{1}{\binom{n}{r-1}}+\frac{1}{\binom{n}{r}+1}$

\begin{array}{l}

\Rightarrow \quad 2=\frac{{ }^{\mathrm{n}} \mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{r}}}{{ }^{\mathrm{n}} \mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{r}-1}}=\frac{{ }^{\mathrm{n}} \mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{r}}}{{ }^{\mathrm{n}} \mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{r}+1}} \\

\Rightarrow \quad 2=\frac{\mathrm{n}-\mathrm{r}+1}{\mathrm{r}}+\frac{\mathrm{r}+1}{\mathrm{n}-\mathrm{r}} \\

\Rightarrow \mathrm{n}^{2}-4 \mathrm{nr}+4 \mathrm{r}^{2}+\mathrm{n}=0 \\

\Rightarrow(\mathrm{n}-2 \mathrm{r})^{2}+\mathrm{n}=0

\end{array}



which is not possible for any value for $n$.

questions.q: If \(\mathrm{p}^{\text {th }}, \mathrm{q}^{\text {th }}\) and \(\mathrm{r}^{\text {th }}\) terms of H.P. are \(\mathrm{u}, \mathrm{v}, \mathrm{w}\) respectively, then find the value of the expression \((q-r) v w+(r-p) w u+(p-q) u v\).
questions.solution:
Let H.P. be \(\frac{1}{\mathrm{a}}+\frac{1}{\mathrm{a}+\mathrm{d}}+\frac{1}{\mathrm{a}+2 \mathrm{~d}}+\ldots \ldots\)
\(\begin{aligned}
& \therefore \mathrm{u}=\frac{1}{\mathrm{a}+(\mathrm{p}-1) \mathrm{d}}, \mathrm{v}=\frac{1}{\mathrm{a}+(\mathrm{q}-1) \mathrm{d}}, \\
& \mathrm{w}=\frac{1}{\mathrm{a}+(\mathrm{r}-1) \mathrm{d}} \Rightarrow \mathrm{a}+(\mathrm{p}-1) \mathrm{d}=\frac{1}{\mathrm{u}} \\
& \mathrm{a}+(\mathrm{q}-1) \mathrm{d}=\frac{1}{\mathrm{v}}, \mathrm{a}+(\mathrm{r}-1) \mathrm{d}=\frac{1}{\mathrm{w}} \\
& \Rightarrow(\mathrm{q}-\mathrm{r})\{\mathrm{a}+(\mathrm{p}-1) \mathrm{d}\}+(\mathrm{r}-\mathrm{p})\{\mathrm{a}+(\mathrm{q}-1) \mathrm{d}\}+\ldots \ldots \\
& =\frac{1}{\mathrm{u}}(\mathrm{q}-\mathrm{r})+\frac{1}{\mathrm{v}}(\mathrm{r}-\mathrm{p})+\ldots . \Rightarrow(q-r) \mathrm{vw}+\ldots . . = 0
\end{aligned}\)

questions.q: The coefficient of \(x^{32}\) in the expansion of \(\left(x^4-\frac{1}{x^3}\right)^{15}\) is:
questions.solution:
We know by Binomial expansion, that \((x+a)^{\mathrm{n}}\)
\(\begin{aligned}
&={ }^{\mathrm{n}} \mathrm{C}_0 x^{\mathrm{n}} \mathrm{a}^0+{ }^{\mathrm{n}} \mathrm{C}_1 \mathrm{x}^{\mathrm{n}-1} \cdot \mathrm{a}+{ }^{\mathrm{n}} \mathrm{C}_2 \mathrm{x}^{\mathrm{n}-2} \mathrm{a}^2 \\
&+{ }^{\mathrm{n}} \mathrm{C}_3 \mathrm{x}^{\mathrm{n}-3} \mathrm{a}^3+{ }^{\mathrm{n}} \mathrm{C}_4 \mathrm{x}^{\mathrm{n}-4} \cdot \mathrm{a}^4+\ldots . .+{ }^{\mathrm{n}} \mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{n}} \mathrm{x}^0 a^{\mathrm{n}}
\end{aligned}\)
Given expansion is \(\left(x^4-\frac{1}{x^3}\right)^{15}\)
On comparing we get \(\mathrm{n}=15, \mathrm{x}=\mathrm{x}^4\),
\(a=\left(-\frac{1}{x^3}\right)\)
\(\begin{aligned}
& \therefore\left(x^4-\frac{1}{x^3}\right)^{15}={ }^{15} \mathrm{C}_0\left(\mathrm{x}^4\right)^{15}\left(-\frac{1}{\mathrm{x}^3}\right)^0 \\
& +{ }^{15} \mathrm{C}_1\left(\mathrm{x}^4\right)^{14}\left(-\frac{1}{\mathrm{x}^3}\right)+{ }^{15} \mathrm{C}_2\left(\mathrm{x}^4\right)^{13}\left(-\frac{1}{\mathrm{x}^3}\right)^2 \\
& +{ }^{15} \mathrm{C}_3\left(\mathrm{x}^4\right)^{12}\left(-\frac{1}{\mathrm{x}^3}\right)^3+{ }^{15} \mathrm{C}_4\left(\mathrm{x}^4\right)^{11}\left(-\frac{1}{\mathrm{x}^3}\right)^4+\ldots \\
& \mathrm{T}_{\mathrm{r}+1}={ }^{15} \mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{r}}\left(\mathrm{x}^4\right)^{15-\mathrm{r}} \cdot\left(-\frac{1}{\mathrm{x}^3}\right)^{\mathrm{r}}=-{ }^{15} \mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{r}} \mathrm{x}^{60-7 \mathrm{r}} \\
& \Rightarrow \mathrm{x}{ }^{60-7 \mathrm{r}}=\mathrm{x}^{32} \Rightarrow 60-7 \mathrm{r}=32 \\
& \Rightarrow 7 \mathrm{r}=28 \Rightarrow \mathrm{r}=4
\end{aligned}\)
So, 5 th term, contains \(\mathrm{x}^{32}\)
\(={ }^{15} C_4\left(x^4\right){ }^{11}\left(-\frac{1}{x^3}\right)^4={ }^{15} C_4 x^{44} x^{-12}\)
\(={ }^{15} \mathrm{C}_4 \mathrm{x}^{32} .\)
Thus, coefficient of \(\mathrm{x}^{32}={ }^{15} \mathrm{C}_4\).

questions.q: If \(A\) and \(B\) are \(2 \times 2\) matrices, then which of the following is true?
questions.solution:
For two \(2 \times 2\) matrices, \(A ~\&~ B\)
\(\begin{aligned}
& (A-B) \times(A+B) \\
& =A \times A+A \times B-B \times A-B \times B \\
& =A^2-B^2+A B-B A
\end{aligned}\)
Hence, \((A-B)(A+B)=A^2+A B-B A-B^2\)
